item.title: Version 1.2.1
item.description:
Fixed

  • Preferences → General shows its "Keyboard Shortcuts" heading again; 1.2.0 had renamed it "Shortcuts". In other languages, the new Shortcuts section in Advanced was headed "Keyboard Shortcuts"; it now reads "Shortcuts".

Documentation

  • A full user manual is now available: https://github.com/purpleax/MeetingView-Updates/blob/main/MANUAL.md
  • Correction to the 1.2.0 notes: the "Between meetings" setting is in Preferences → Display & Events.

item.title: Version 1.2.0
item.description:
Added

  • Free time in the menu bar: between meetings it shows "Free for 1h 20m" or "Free until 14:30" instead of the next meeting, which comes back 10 minutes before it starts. Choose the style, or turn it off, under Settings → Appearance → "Between meetings".
  • Overlapping and back-to-back meetings are marked in the menu, with the other meeting named when you hover.
  • Shortcuts and Siri actions: "Join Next Meeting", "Get Next Meeting" (title, times, link, service, calendar and location) and "Time Until Next Meeting". Ask Siri, for example, "What's my next meeting in MeetingView".
  • Run a Shortcut when a meeting starts or ends, for example to turn on a Focus, mute notifications or set your status. Pick them under Settings → Advanced → Shortcuts. The Shortcut receives the meeting's details.

item.title: Version 1.1.4
item.description:
Removed

  • The "What's New" menu item and window. Release notes are still shown in the update window when a new version is available, and on each GitHub release.

item.title: Version 1.1.3
item.description:
Changed

  • Google Calendar is only offered when the build has a Google sign-in client. Releases don't have one yet, so they offer macOS Calendar only, which also shows Google calendars added to Calendar.app. Before, choosing Google Calendar ended in a "not configured" error.

Fixed

  • Saving the Google session can no longer delete the saved one if the keychain write fails.
  • The signed-in Google account's email address is now read correctly.
  • Google sign-out sends the revoke request correctly encoded, and keychain failures are logged.

Security

  • Google Calendar responses are no longer kept in an on-disk cache that outlived sign-out.

item.title: Version 1.1.2
item.description:
Security

  • Links from calendar invites only open if they're web links or Zoom or Discord app links. An invite can no longer make MeetingView open a file share, a local file or another app's link, including through a Google redirect, the event's URL field or a broad custom regex.
  • Lookalike hosts such as evilzoom.us or meetXgoogle.com are no longer treated as Zoom or Google Meet, so they don't get a real service's icon, a Zoom app rewrite or your email address added to the link.
  • A custom browser set as a plain program only ever receives web links.
  • Very large or crafted invite descriptions can no longer stall the app: HTML handling and link detection now take time in proportion to the text, and only the first 64 KB of a description is scanned.
  • Updates: the update feed is now signed with the same key as the downloads, and MeetingView refuses a feed without a valid signature. Someone who could change the feed can no longer push an older version or hold back updates.

item.title: Version 1.1.1
item.description:
Fixed

  • A routine update check that finds nothing new is no longer logged as an error.

item.title: Version 1.1.0
item.description:
Added

  • Automatic updates: MeetingView checks for new versions once a day and can download and install them for you. Updates are signed and notarized, and are verified before they're installed.
  • "Check for Updates…" in the menu, and an Updates section in Settings → General with the current version, when it last checked, and options to check and install automatically.
